source_text: Et quod persuasit diabolus tenuiter, sollerter et perseveranter fingit et protegit et custodit et format Deus.
pass_a_gloss: And what the devil has persuaded thinly, God skillfully and perseveringly fashions and protects and guards and forms.
pass_b_english: And what the devil weakly persuaded someone to do, God skillfully and persistently fashions, protects, preserves, and forms.

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
